newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat approval ratings up - poll.
newsitem.headline: Arafat approval ratings up - poll.

text.p: Palestinian approval of Yasser Arafat has grown since recent Israeli-Palestinian clashes, according to an opinion poll released on Thursday.
The Jerusalem Media and Communication Centre (JMCC) poll put Palestinian President Arafat's approval rating at 68 percent, up eleven points from a poll by the same group three months ago.

Seventy-seven percent of the poll's respondents said that September clashes, pitting Palestinian civilians and police against Israeli troops, benefited the Palestinian cause. Ninety percent approved of the intervention of PLO security forces in the clashes. Fifty-six percent said the Palestinian self-rule Authority had made effective use of the unrest.

Protests by stone-throwing Palestinian civilians, spurred by Israeli policies in Jerusalem in September, escalated into running gunbattles between Palestinian police and Israeli troops, killing 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis.
JMCC conducted 1,199 face-to-face interviews in the West Bank and Gaza Strip on October 24 and 25. The poll had a margin of error of 3 percent.
